title: GEAR: Feature-Based Configuration and Code Generation for Agentic Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.35592v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Engineering multi-agent systems (MAS) requires choosing agents, orchestration strategies, communication mechanisms, reasoning approaches, and memory configurations. These choices depend on framework-specific capabilities and abstractions, requiring developers to learn different APIs when exploring alternative implementations. We present GEAR, an open-source tool for configuring MAS and generating framework-specific implementations from a common specification. GEAR uses a feature-based representation to make configuration options and their constraints explicit, enabling users to validate specifications before code generation. Through connectors for ten agentic frameworks, users generate projects from the same specification and can then inspect reports describing framework-specific adaptations. A preliminary assessment of mapping feasibility identifies translation strategies for 271 of 320 evaluated feature-framework pairs (84.69%). GEAR

translated_title: GEAR：面向智能体系统的基于特征的配置与代码生成
translated_abstract: 构建多智能体系统（MAS）需要选择智能体、编排策略、通信机制、推理方法和记忆配置。这些选择依赖于特定框架的能力和抽象，导致开发者在探索不同实现方案时需要学习不同的API。我们提出了GEAR，这是一个开源工具，用于配置多智能体系统，并能从统一的规范生成特定框架的实现。GEAR采用基于特征的表示方式，使配置选项及其约束显式化，从而支持用户在代码生成前对规范进行验证。通过为十个智能体框架提供的连接器，用户可以从同一规范生成项目，并随后查看描述框架特定适配情况的报告。对映射可行性的初步评估显示，在320个被评估的特征-框架对中，有271个（84.69%）确定了相应的翻译策略。
tldr: GEAR是一个开源工具，通过基于特征的统一规范来配置多智能体系统，并能自动生成适用于十个不同智能体框架的代码实现，解决了开发者需要学习不同框架API的问题。
en_tdlr: GEAR is an open-source tool that enables configuring multi-agent systems through a feature-based common specification and automatically generating framework-specific implementations across ten agentic frameworks.
